Subject: Data retention - default capture for requests/outputs/derivatives

Hi David / Laura,

We're wrapping up our vendor risk review and need a concise statement of what Redwood retains by default for the hosted API. Specifically Brightbank needs clarity on: request inputs (raw prompts), model outputs, system messages / prompts, ephemeral artifacts (streaming fragments, KV cache), embeddings, and whether any of these are retained longer for debugging or quality purposes.

Can you provide a simple table or bullets (what is kept by default, retention window, where the data lives, and how a customer can opt-out or request deletion)? Also, please attach any SOC2 excerpts that mention telemetry/retention.

Thanks — tight timeline on our side, so a short, precise answer is ideal.

Best,

Hi Eleanor — thanks for the clear ask. Short version below; attaching a one-page retention matrix for detail and an SOC2 excerpt per your request. Happy to hop on a 20m call if you want to walk through specifics for Brightbank.

Summary (hosted Redwood API - defaults):
- Raw request inputs (user prompts, uploaded text/files references): retained 30 days by default for troubleshooting and rate-limiting analysis. Stored in our telemetry store (customer-scoped).
- Model outputs (generated tokens/responses): retained 90 days by default to support quality investigations and regression analysis.
- System prompts & instruction templates (customer-provided or account-level system messages): retained 365 days by default to support reproducibility of results; customers can delete or rotate templates via the Console.
- Streaming fragments (partial tokens emitted during streaming) and KV cache entries used for live sessions: ephemeral — retained for session duration + 24 hours, then purged automatically. Not included in long-term telemetry unless explicitly saved.
- Embeddings: not retained by default as searchable indices. CreateEmbeddings API calls return vectors; storing them into an index is an opt-in action by the customer (we do not index or persist embeddings beyond the API response unless the customer creates an index or enables long-term vector storage).
- Derivative artifacts (logs for reranking, eval snapshots, annotated outputs): retained per artifact type — default is 90 days unless the customer enables longer-term retention for audits or eval comparisons.

Opt-out & deletion paths:
1) Account setting: customers can toggle "retain_request_data" in the Console to opt out of request-level telemetry; setting that to false reduces default retention windows for new requests to 0 days (no long-term storage) — note: short-term operational buffers still exist for brief routing and rate-limit enforcement.
2) Immediate deletion: customers may open a support ticket with type=deletion-request and provide the date ranges and identifiers; we run the standard deletion runbook and issue a deletion certificate when completed.
3) Private/Dedicated option: For customers needing full control, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) allows customers to manage all retention locally.

Exceptions and caveats:
- Aggregated telemetry and anonymous metrics used for service health are kept longer (up to 24 months) and are non-identifying.
- If a customer enables any evaluative feature that snapshots inputs+outputs into a persisted eval corpus, those snapshots follow the eval retention setting (defaults to 365 days).
- Legal holds: we will not delete data subject to a valid legal hold or subpoena until release.

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix.xlsx (one-page defaults + opt-out steps), SOC2-excerpt-2025.pdf (section on telemetry & logging).

If useful, I can convert the bullets above into a one-page table formatted for Brightbank's vendor pack.

Regards,

Eleanor — looped in Laura and Kimberly for the few clarifications; updated answer below (we also attached the matrix and a SOC2 excerpt).

Final concise table (for vendor pack):
- Raw requests (prompts, file references): default retention = 30 days; stored in customer-scoped telemetry; opt-out via Console toggle "retain_request_data" = false (prevents long-term persistence of new requests).
- Model outputs (generated text): default retention = 90 days; used for debugging, quality, and regression detection; can be deleted on request.
- System prompts & templates: default retention = 365 days; managed in account templates and removable by customer admins.
- Streaming & KV cache: ephemeral; session + 24 hours retention; not stored to long-term telemetry by default.
- Embeddings: not retained as indices by default; persisting vectors requires an explicit index creation call (index retention default = 365 days if enabled).
- Eval/derivative snapshots: default retention = 90 days unless eval persistence is enabled (365 days).

Notes:
- Short-term operational buffers (seconds - minutes) exist to ensure request routing and rate-limiting; toggles prevent long-term storage but do not remove transient in-flight state.
- For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; we can provide a data-handling attestation for procurement.
